arChildNodes.szComment: PLAYER: "Have you lost your mind? You could have been killed!"
Crouching to speak with Lorath, looking him in the eye
Lorath tears off his Horadric Talisman, drops it on the ground, and limps away.

EXT. ABANDONED FOLLOWER ENCAMPMENT - NIGHT 

Flames ROAR over the tents. The air is thick with smoke, speckled with dancing embers. 

The Player kneels and looks down at— 

The HORADRIC PENDANT in the dirt. 

The Player is torn about what to do. The fact Lorath would put aside his pendant is serious. 

A CROW CAWS, drawing the Player’s attention. They look up and see -  

Multiple CAWING CROWS flying in the direction of Lorath. 

The Player knows their friend is in danger. They stand, and we CUT TO:

Lorath stops short, shakes his head. What’s the point anyway? He plops down on the ground, wincing at his wound. He stares ahead. He’s demoralized, defeated. A shell. 

A Crow hops into frame, CAWING. Then another. And another. 

Lorath regards the crows – not with anger, but with grim acceptance.
The Player rushes forward and waves at the Crows. They hope away, but they don’t fly off. They CAW in protest.

Suddenly, AN EXPLOSION OF LIGHT RIPS THROUGH THE CAMP. IT INCINERATES THE CROWS AND SNUFFS OUT THE SURROUNDING FLAMES. 

What the hell was that? 

Player and Lorath both whirl, searching for where the source of the light came from. Beautiful embers of glowing light drift around them like tiny falling stars. 

Lorath stands, still wincing in pain, and shocked. He’s hearing the voice of a ghost—someone he hasn’t seen in years. It can’t be real, can it? 

He turns toward the source of the voice and sees - 

A HOODED FIGURE APPROACHING. AN OTHERWORLDLY VISAGE. WHISPS OF SMOKE AND LIGHT TRAIL OFF THE STRANGER LIKE AN ANGEL’S WINGS. Is it an angel? A monster? We don’t know yet. 

The Player moves in front of Lorath to protect him. 

The newcomer removes his hood. Lorath is shocked to see -
Lorath edges past the Player, toward Tyrael. But his awe soon withers into suspicion. He shakes his head, rubs his hand over his face.
He stomps toward Tyrael, lifts his torch high, readying to strike this “phantom.”

Tyrael holds out a fist, then opens it. 

The Horadric Pendant lies in his palm. 

Lorath stares at it, then up at Tyrael. The flame on the torch gutters, extinguishes.

And he slowly takes the Pendant from Tyrael’s hand. 

This is no illusion.

Lorath grips his wounded side and falls unconscious – he falls into Tyrael. And the mortal angel catches him.  

The Player rushes forward to be at Lorath’s side. As Tyrael lowers the old Horadrim to the ground, he looks at the Player – the two of them share a look.  

A silent shared concern for this troubled man they both deeply care for.
